page.answer: Short answer. The best 120/240 split phase hybrid solar inverter for most homes in 2026 is the EG4 18kPV: 12 kW, a 200 A bypass and a generator input in one box, and it idled at 60–70 W in The Solar Lab's tests against 97 W for the Sol-Ark 15K. The FlexBOSS21 idled at 65 W.

page.after:
What the differences mean

An inverter draws its idle power every hour it is switched on, so small wattage differences add up:

  • EG4 18kPV: 60–70 W × 24 h = 1.44–1.68 kWh a day.
  • EG4 FlexBOSS21: 65 W × 24 h = 1.56 kWh a day.
  • Sol-Ark 15K-2P: 97 W × 24 h = 2.33 kWh a day. Against the FlexBOSS21 that is (97 − 65) W × 8,760 h ≈ 280 kWh a year.
  • A whole-home 200 A install with the FlexBOSS21 needs EG4's GridBOSS: $3,599.99 + $1,799.99 = $5,399.98 before breakers. That is $1,399.99 more than the 18kPV, which has its 200 A bypass built in.
  • Price per kW of battery output: 18kPV $3,999.99 ÷ 12 kW ≈ $333; FlexBOSS21 + GridBOSS $5,399.98 ÷ 12 kW ≈ $450; Sol-Ark 15K-2P $5,650 ÷ 13 kW ≈ $435; 6000XP $1,499.99 ÷ 6 kW = $250.

Idle draw: what a hybrid inverter burns doing nothing

A hybrid inverter keeps its power stage, control boards and fans running whenever it is on, whether the house is drawing 50 W or 5 kW. On a grid-tied system the grid covers most of that loss. During an outage or off-grid it comes straight out of the battery, including overnight when there is no solar to replace it.

The Solar Lab tested each of these units in a separate review:

  • Sol-Ark 15K-2P: an idle draw of 97 W in standby. In the same review it started a 10,000 W surge compressor while already at its full 15 kW load, and did it twice. That is the strongest surge result in this group.
  • EG4 FlexBOSS21: about 65 W in The Solar Lab's idle tests. In the same comparison the Sol-Ark 18K idled at about 108 W.
  • EG4 18kPV: about 1.2 A from the battery, or 60–70 W. It also ran a 15 kW heater on battery alone and charged its battery at 11,400 W against a 12,000 W rating.
  • EG4 6000XP: 0.9–1.2 A from the battery, in line with EG4's 50 W rating.

Over a 12-hour night, the gap between the Sol-Ark 15K-2P and the 18kPV is 27–37 W × 12 h = 0.32–0.44 kWh of battery. The Solar Lab does not publish an instrument or method for these readings, and each figure comes from a separate review, so treat differences under about 10 W as a tie.

Not recommended

The EG4 6000XP as a grid-tied hybrid. Signature Solar describes it as running independently of the grid or using grid input only for charging, so it does not sell power back. EG4's 6000XP manual (v1.2) lists 3,000 W maximum continuous per line against 6,000 W nominal. Put 4,000 W of 120 V appliances on one leg and you are 1,000 W over that leg's limit, even though the house total is under 6 kW. Buy it only for an off-grid panel whose legs you can balance. For a small off-grid build on a tighter budget, Sun Gold Power's SPH6548P costs $1,035 at Sun Gold Power (2026-11-13) for 6,500 W rated and 13,000 VA peak. Its UL 1741 listing covers off-grid systems only, so it is not a grid-tied hybrid either: {buy:sungoldpower-sph6548p-6-5kw-48v-hybrid-inverter}
